newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares finish mixed in light holiday trading.
newsitem.headline: KL shares finish mixed in light holiday trading.

text.p: Kuala Lumpur share prices ended a narrow-ranged session mixed in light holiday business, with small-capitalisation issues giving up some of Thursday's sharp gains in profit-taking.

"There wasn't a great deal of action," said an institutional dealer with a local securities firm. "A few of my clients said their books are closed. The volume is poor in terms of stock participation."
After trading within a five-point band, the blue chip focused Composite Index ended up 1.32 points to 1,209.00. The Second Board index eased 3.52 points to 563.71.
The Second Board index had surged over four percent on Thursday. Overall turnover remained lacklustre at 116 million shares, compared with 106 million on Thursday. Losers led gainers by 283 to 249.
Next week's trading looks slow as well, dealers said. "I think it's going to be quiet," said Leong Yoon Siang, of TA Seecurities' international division.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange, the spot December contract was up 0.8 points to 1,200.0 on volume of 197 lots, while the January futures contract was up 1.5 to 1,207.5 with 157 lots traded.
